claim: In 2026 El Puerto de Santa María holds Blue Flags on four beaches (Fuentebravía, La Puntilla, Santa Catalina/Vistahermosa-Las Redes, Valdelagrana) plus Puerto Sherry marina.
quote: criterios como la calidad del agua, la gestión ambiental, la accesibilidad o los servicios disponibles

claim: Valdelagrana is an urban Blue Flag beach 1,880m long and 85m wide with hammock rentals, food and a children's zone; La Puntilla is 1,300m with surf; Fuentebravía 700m semi-urban with surf/diving; Santa Catalina (Vistahermosa) 3,000m long; La Calita is the smallest at 590m with diving.
Playa La Puntilla sits at the mouth of the Guadalete river, separated from it by a breakwater, with calm bathing waters, accessibility for reduced mobility and over 100 parking spaces.
quote: La Puntilla ... desembocadura del río Guadalete ... aguas tranquilas para el baño

claim: Playa La Calita has a wild appearance with rocky outcrops in the water and sand, making it good for spearfishing and scuba diving, and does not hold a Blue Flag.
quote: aspecto salvaje ... rocas ... ideal para la pesca submarina y el buceo

claim: Puerto Sherry is a marina and yacht club in the Bay of Cádiz offering moorings, boat rentals and waterfront facilities, a hub for nautical activity.
quote: Puerto Sherry | Marina & Yacht Club in El Puerto de Santa María

claim: Private boat trips depart Puerto Sherry's dock M with an accredited skipper, sailing to Valdelagrana to anchor, swim and do paddle surf on a roughly three-hour outing.
quote: Meeting at dock M in Puerto Sherry ... sailing to Valdelagrana beach where you can drop anchor ... paddle surfing and water sports

claim: The Sendero Pinar de la Algaida is a 12km round-trip walk through stone-pine forest and marshland skirting a saltpan, best done September to May at low tide with binoculars for birds.
quote: 12km ... Pinar de la Algaida, a forest of stone pines ... best time to walk is from September to May, at low tide

claim: Bahía de Cádiz Natural Park spans ~10,522 hectares across five municipalities including El Puerto de Santa María, with the untouched Pinar del Coto de la Isleta pine forest, salt flats and mudflats hosting over 50,000 aquatic birds including flamingos, spoonbills, terns and avocets.
quote: populations of more than 50,000 aquatic birds, with flamingos among the notable species
